initial.policy:
# open-nitpick's own review configuration. It is also the worked example the
# README points at, so it stays readable rather than exhaustive.

models:
  # Synthetic's built-in endpoint lets committed policy select models without
  # storing credentials. Set SYNTHETIC_API_KEY in the environment or keystore.
  default:
    provider: synthetic
    model: hf:zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash

  triage:
    provider: synthetic
    model: hf:Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B
    temperature: 0

  # Editing quality has not been measured; fixes still require review and CI.
  fix:
    provider: synthetic
    model: hf:moonshotai/Kimi-K3
    temperature: 0

review:
  # Advisory: this project reviews itself, and a false positive should not
  # block its own PRs.
  fail_on: none
  min_severity: info
  concurrency: 4
  # A million-token model can read far more than 60k tokens per request; the
  # budget is about how much one call is asked to judge at once, not what
  # the model can hold. Raised here, where the reviewer is a frontier model.
  token_budget_per_request: 120000
  # Definitions the change imports are attached by default. The caller
  # walk, which reads files the change never named, is off by default and
  # on here, where reviews are advisory and the repository is this one;
  # docs/findings.md's callers section is the evidence for what it finds.
  related_context: true
  related_context_callers: true
  ignore:
    # Generated vectors, not source. `nitpick knowledge-index` writes them and
    # a test checks them against the corpus, so a reviewer reading them can
    # find nothing a person would act on. The 4096-dimension bundle is 393k
    # tokens on its own, which is three times this file's per-request budget:
    # it does not fail to be worth reviewing, it fails to be reviewable, and
    # the batch that tried it failed the run.
    - "internal/knowledge/indexes/**"
    - "notes/evidence/**"

instructions:
  - path: "**/*.go"
    prompt: >-
      Flag unchecked errors, ignored context cancellation, and goroutines that
      can outlive their caller. Do not comment on formatting or naming.

  - path: "internal/diff/**"
    prompt: >-
      This package maps diff lines to review-comment anchors. An off-by-one
      here misplaces every comment in a file, so treat any change to position
      or line-number arithmetic as high risk and reason about it explicitly.

  - path: "internal/llm/**"
    prompt: >-
      This package must keep working across providers with very different
      capabilities. Flag anything that assumes a provider supports tools,
      JSON-schema response formats, or a particular error shape.

  - path: "**/*_test.go"
    prompt: >-
      Judge whether the test would actually fail if the behavior it describes
      broke. Do not ask for more tests for their own sake.

linters:
  mode: auto
  enabled: [golangci-lint]
  only_changed_lines: true

practices:
  profile: ""
  # Models still run in reviews; only deterministic completion gates CI.
  required: [conventions, linters, commits, slop-tells]
  required_conventions:
    - go-doc-comment-name
    - go-error-wrap
    - go-ctx-first-arg
    - go-no-naked-return
    - go-test-name-sentence
    - go-test-helper-marks
  boundaries:
    - from: github.com/jdziat/open-nitpick/internal/commits
      forbid: [os/exec, net/http]
      reason: Commit subject validation must not launch processes or make HTTP requests.
    - from: github.com/jdziat/open-nitpick/internal/standards
      forbid: [os/exec, net/http]
      reason: Convention probes measure supplied source; analyzers run in internal/linters.

validation:
  enabled: true

- `notes/engineering-acceptance-audit.md:70` — Audit section contradicts schema field requirement
  - Data durability and migration expert: The change under review modifies only this audit markdown, no schema file or description rewrite appears anywhere in the diff, and the added section itself frames the conditional revised_severity requirement as outstanding work ("Clarify the conditional requirement… Resolve this before relying on a full internal required-model run"). cmd/nitpick/engineering_model.go:56
  **⚪ nit · consistency**
  
  Prompt version literal repeated across two files
  
  The same prompt version string appears in four check literals and in the prompt text. A later bump that misses one site leaves an entry point attributing findings to a prompt version that did not produce them. A package-level constant beside engineeringPrompt reduces the next bump to one edit plus the prompt text.
  
  <sub>flagged by synthetic/hf:zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash · triaged by synthetic/hf:Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B</sub>

internal/review/acknowledgement_eval_test.go:108
  **⚪ nit · general**
  
  Call counter on the eval recorder is never read
  
  The counter is incremented on every GenerateContent call but no assertion or log line reads it, so the harness pins nothing about how many model calls triage issues. A reader auditing the eval harness has to trace the field to learn the count is unchecked; if it was meant to pin one call per triage run, that assertion is missing.
  
  <sub>flagged by synthetic/hf:zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash · triaged by synthetic/hf:Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B</sub>

internal/review/acknowledgement_eval_test.go:108
  **⚪ nit · structure**
  
  acknowledgementRecorder call counter is never read
  
  calls is incremented on every GenerateContent, but no assertion, log, or failure message reads it. Eval output never shows the count, and nothing catches a change in how many calls triage makes. Drop the field and increment, or log the value next to raw_response.
  
  <sub>flagged by synthetic/hf:zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash · triaged by synthetic/hf:Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B</sub>

internal/review/schema.go:220
  **⚪ nit · structure**
  
  Composite literal field order differs from struct
  
  The literal initializes Reason before RevisedSeverity, while the struct declaration and JSON output order use the opposite order. Verifying the emitted key order requires reconciling two orderings of the same fields. Align the literal with the struct declaration.
  
  <sub>flagged by synthetic/hf:zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash · triaged by synthetic/hf:Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B</sub>
  
  Suggested change:
  
  ```
  		RevisedSeverity: map[string]any{
  			"type":        "string",
  			"enum":        severityEnum,
  			"description": "Required when verdict is severity: the explicit level the demonstrated consequence supports. Omit for other verdicts. A severity verdict without this value is invalid.",
  		},
  		Reason: map[string]any{
  			"type": "string",
  			"description": "One or two sentences. For a refutation this is the specific reason the claim " +
  				"is wrong; uncertainty is not a reason.",
  		},
  ```

notes/triage-acknowledgements.md:3
  **⚪ nit · style**
  
  Status line adds another name for controls
  
  The replacement status wording uses protocol controls, while the file also uses live controls and synthetic controls for the same suite. A reader matching the status claim to the runnable command or evidence files must infer that all names denote one suite.
  
  <sub>flagged by synthetic/hf:zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash · triaged by synthetic/hf:Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B</sub>
